Across the four responses, the core identification of "nation or people" is never the primary meaning; it is consistently listed among the common alternatives. The book's statement therefore preserves the general referent (great trees as symbols of nations or empires) but materially narrows its extension to the specific case of a nation or people.  

This is a REFINED  relationship. The book's core remains inside the consensus cluster; it simply excludes the other senses (righteous person, Tree of Life, cross, moral character, etc.) that the broader tradition treats as equally attested. The citations supplied with the entry supply partial support, since they are already present in the consensus alternatives.

No contradiction at the core level, only boundary tightening.  

The book's claim is therefore recognizable mainstream but not the settled consensus primary. It is a legitimate refinement rather than a novel or divergent reading. The printed citations alone give partial support, as they match the kingdom/people alternative but do not address the other senses the consensus lists.
